questions.text: List the boundaries of the 3rd ventricle.
questions.explanation: This is a long-answer anatomy question from the CNS module; a complete response should cover the points outlined in the model answer. It is classified under the chapter 'Diencephalon, Reticular Formation, Sleep & Epilepsy'.
questions.keyConcept: The boundaries of the 3rd ventricle.
questions.modelAnswer:
Boundaries of the third ventricle: It is a median slit-like cavity between the two thalami and hypothalami. Anteriorly – the lamina terminalis, the anterior commissure and the columns of the fornix. Posteriorly – the pineal body, the posterior commissure and the opening of the cerebral aqueduct. Roof – the ependyma and the tela choroidea (with the choroid plexus) stretched between the two thalami, beneath the body of the fornix and corpus callosum. Floor – from before backward: the optic chiasma, infundibulum/tuber cinereum, mammillary bodies, posterior perforated substance and the tegmentum of the midbrain. Lateral wall – the medial surface of the thalamus (above) and the hypothalamus (below), separated by the hypothalamic sulcus, joined across the cavity by the interthalamic adhesion (connexus).

questions.text: Describe anterior thalamic nuclei.
questions.explanation: This is a long-answer anatomy question from the CNS module; a complete response should cover the points outlined in the model answer. It is classified under the chapter 'Diencephalon, Reticular Formation, Sleep & Epilepsy'.
questions.keyConcept: Anterior thalamic nuclei.
questions.modelAnswer:
Anterior thalamic nuclei: They lie within the anterior tubercle of the thalamus (within the bifurcation of the internal medullary lamina). They receive the mammillothalamic tract (from the mammillary body) and project to the cingulate gyrus. They form part of the limbic system (Papez circuit) and are concerned with emotion, behaviour and recent memory.

questions.keyConcept: Lateral part of thalamus & its nuclei.
questions.modelAnswer:
Lateral part of the thalamus and its nuclei: The lateral nuclear mass is divided into a dorsal tier (lateral dorsal, lateral posterior and pulvinar nuclei – association nuclei connected with the parietal/occipital/temporal association cortex) and a ventral tier: the ventral anterior (VA) and ventral lateral (VL) nuclei (motor relay – from the basal ganglia and cerebellum to the motor cortex), and the ventral posterior nucleus – ventral posterolateral (VPL, body sensation via medial and spinal lemnisci) and ventral posteromedial (VPM, face sensation and taste) – relaying to the somatosensory cortex.

questions.explanation: This is a long-answer anatomy question from the CNS module; a complete response should cover the points outlined in the model answer. It is classified under the chapter 'Diencephalon, Reticular Formation, Sleep & Epilepsy'.
questions.keyConcept: Non-specific thalamic nuclei.
questions.modelAnswer:
Non-specific thalamic nuclei: These are nuclei with diffuse cortical and reticular connections (not relaying a specific modality). They include the intralaminar nuclei (notably the centromedian and parafascicular nuclei, within the internal medullary lamina), the midline nuclei, and the reticular nucleus of the thalamus. They are connected with the reticular formation and the striatum and are concerned with arousal, alerting and the maintenance of consciousness, and with the perception of pain.

Blood supply of the thalamus: It is supplied mainly by branches of the posterior cerebral and posterior communicating arteries: the thalamoperforating (paramedian) arteries, the thalamogeniculate arteries, and the posterior choroidal arteries; the anterior part is supplied by the polar (tuberothalamic) artery from the posterior communicating artery. questions.text: Enumerate functions of hypothalamus.
questions.explanation: This is a long-answer anatomy question from the CNS module; a complete response should cover the points outlined in the model answer. It is classified under the chapter 'Diencephalon, Reticular Formation, Sleep & Epilepsy'.
questions.keyConcept: Functions of hypothalamus.
questions.modelAnswer:
Functions of the hypothalamus: (1) Control of the autonomic nervous system (anterior part = parasympathetic, posterior part = sympathetic). (2) Control of the endocrine system through the pituitary gland (releasing/inhibiting hormones and the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei producing ADH and oxytocin). (3) Regulation of body temperature. (4) Regulation of food and water intake (hunger, satiety and thirst centres). (5) Regulation of emotional and sexual behaviour (part of the limbic system). (6) Regulation of the biological clock (circadian rhythm) and the sleep-wake cycle.

questions.text: Describe communications of hypothalamus with pituitary gland.
questions.explanation: This is a long-answer anatomy question from the CNS module; a complete response should cover the points outlined in the model answer. It is classified under the chapter 'Diencephalon, Reticular Formation, Sleep & Epilepsy'.
questions.keyConcept: Communications of hypothalamus with pituitary gland.
questions.modelAnswer:
Communications of the hypothalamus with the pituitary gland: (1) With the posterior lobe (neurohypophysis) by a NERVOUS connection – the hypothalamo-hypophyseal tract, whose axons arise in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei and pass down the infundibulum to release ADH (vasopressin) and oxytocin from the posterior lobe. (2) With the anterior lobe (adenohypophysis) by a VASCULAR connection – the hypothalamo-hypophyseal portal system, which carries releasing and inhibiting hormones from the median eminence/tuber cinereum to control the secretion of the anterior pituitary hormones.
